modules.name: City in Nature scorecard and evidence ledger
modules.effort: M: about 4-5 person-days (schema, force-aware radar, ledger, views panel); needs M02-M08 outputs and SITE views
modules.design_question: Does the scheme give space for nature on buildings and sites and keep views and connections to mountains and water, and which claims rest on binding rules versus targets, guidelines, comparators or team assumptions?
inputs: Typed metric records from P05-M02..M08: {value, unit, good, bad, status, force, source_ids}
Layer 0: site polygon (default 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2), storey levels and program tags
SITE public-views module: QE Park view cone status, protected view corridors, mountain-ridgeline views kept or blocked
User settings: target set, R019 site type A/B/C, optional weights (default none), Park Board dedication flag
outputs: P05.Scorecard JSON (per indicator: value, threshold, status, force, source id, ODP direction, jury tag)
Radar + ledger + two-half City in Nature panel SVG for the policy-reflection board
Evidence ledger CSV (course requirement: every result cites its source)
RPSLD checklist flags: tree and soils strategy (A.4.1), park dedication (A.3.1), food assets (B), water balance (D), groundwater (E)

parameters.name: Indicator set
parameters.relationship: Each indicator maps to L2.3.1 half (a) space for nature and to an ODP Ecology direction (4.1 embed, 4.2 make space, 4.3 protect, 4.4 access); removing one removes the evidence the board can claim for that direction.

parameters.name: Protected views input (L2.3.1 half b)
parameters.relationship: Massing decides which protected mountain and water views and the QE Park view cone stay clear; the SITE module reports kept or blocked and M01 shows it beside the nature indicators, tagged cultural context.

parameters.name: Force class of each indicator
parameters.relationship: Sets how a result is drawn: by-law and rezoning-policy requirements count as pass/fail; targets, guidelines and City aspirations are reference rings; comparators, heuristics and team assumptions are dashed rings with origin.

parameters.name: Site type (R019 A/B/C)
parameters.relationship: R019 describes Type C as a single parcel over an excavated parkade that occasionally qualifies under the Higher Buildings Policy (10-15% canopy); several towers under separate permits suggest Type B (15-20%), so classification can flip pass or fail.

parameters.name: Target set / jurisdiction preset
parameters.relationship: Switching from Vancouver-only to comparators (Toronto, UBC) changes thresholds and relabels them comparator or team assumption, because Vancouver has no equivalent numeric rule.

parameters.name: Weights
parameters.relationship: Raising one weight moves the composite toward that indicator; no City source assigns weights, so any composite is a team assumption and is hidden by default.

parameters.name: Park dedication flag (RPSLD A.3.1)
parameters.relationship: The Park Board decides dedication case by case and may require it on a site this size; dedicated land removes buildable area and changes soil, canopy and access-to-nature results, so the flag links to PUBL.

metrics.name: Binding-requirement indicators passed
metrics.good: All by-law and rezoning-policy-requirement indicators pass
metrics.bad: Any such indicator fails (shown red with clause link)
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption (tool rule). Counts only bylaw_requirement and rezoning_policy_requirement records, so targets, guidelines and heuristics never read as compliance.
metrics.method: Count pass flags from M02-M08 where force is bylaw_requirement or rezoning_policy_requirement

metrics.name: Reference indicators shown (not pass/fail)
metrics.good: Every target, guideline, aspiration, comparator and heuristic drawn with a force label and origin
metrics.bad: Any shown without a force label, or scored as compliance
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption (tool rule). rezoning_target, voluntary_guideline and city_aspiration are dotted reference rings; comparator, heuristic and team items are dashed.
metrics.method: Group records by force; ring style follows force

metrics.name: Source coverage of displayed thresholds
metrics.good: 100% carry a source id or an explicit TEAM ASSUMPTION label
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption (tool rule). Course rule: cite sources, show work, separate delegated from human judgment.
metrics.method: Lint the ledger before export

metrics.name: ODP Ecology direction coverage (4.1-4.4)
metrics.good: Each direction has at least one evidenced indicator or a written human-judgment note
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption (tool rule). Directions are verified ODP text; the coverage rule is the team's.
metrics.method: Join indicator-to-direction table

metrics.name: Protected-view retention (L2.3.1 half b)
metrics.good: No protected view or QE Park view cone intrusion, or a written rationale for each
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. City cites views and connections as half of City in Nature (HBPR p.6); Public Views Guidelines (10 Jul 2024) not opened; Higher Buildings Policy covers buildings entering QE Park view.
metrics.method: Read the SITE views result per protected view

modules.method: Collect each module's records with force and status. Plot an uncapped signed margin m = (value - threshold) / threshold, sign flipped where lower is better; zero-threshold counts plot as pass/fail. Draw by-law and policy thresholds as solid rings, targets and guidelines as dotted, comparators, heuristics and team assumptions as dashed, each labelled with origin. Default view is the ledger with raw values, not one score; a weighted composite exists only if the user sets weights and is labelled TEAM ASSUMPTION. Map each indicator to L2.3.1 half (a) and an ODP direction; show half (b) from the SITE views input. List park dedication, food assets, soils strategy and groundwater as rezoning checklist flags. Non-computable items become human-judgment cards with rationale and author.
visualization: Radar of signed margins, one axis per indicator; solid ring = by-law or policy threshold, dotted = target or guideline, dashed = comparator, heuristic or team assumption; FALSE ASSUMPTION entries in flag colour, kept visible
Evidence ledger table: indicator | value | threshold | force | status badge | clickable source clause
Two-half City in Nature panel (space for nature from M02-M07; views and connections from SITE and M08) with ODP 4.1-4.4 coverage strip and gaps
modules.human_judgment: Whether the scheme achieves City in Nature is a cultural and design judgment: reconciliation, Indigenous perspectives, the meaning of Stanley Park, the water and the mountains, view trade-offs, and whether a justified breach deserves reward cannot be scored.
modules.limits: HBPR p.6 cites ODP policy L2.3.1, but the clause was not found in the adopted or draft ODP text (only FG-numbered policies), so its location is unverified. Composite and weights are team constructs; Map 7 corridors are conceptual.

modules.name: Tree canopy, soil volume and vegetative cover
modules.design_question: How much credited tree canopy and vegetation at maturity does the site carry at grade, podium and tower terraces, and is there enough soil volume under each tree to earn that credit?
inputs: Site.Boundary (Polygon2D, m)
Layer0.Planting[] (Polygon2D + level + onStructure flag + growing-medium depth + soffit/cantilever overlap flag)
Layer0.Trees[] (Point + species preset: mature crown diameter and size class)
Optional baseline: City public-trees dataset and LiDAR 2022 canopy
outputs: P05.Canopy {credited_canopy_m2 by level, canopy_pct, grade_canopy_pct, vegetative_cover_pct, tree_count, soil_volume_per_tree[], crown_credit_factor[]}
Landscaped-area polygons for P05-M04 and continuous-soil vs on-structure split (R019 1.2.3; RPSLD A.4.1 overlay sheets)
Credited canopy shade polygons for P05-M06; planting patches for P05-M07
depends_on: Optional CLIM: sun-hours (shade effect on tree viability)

parameters.name: Mature crown diameter / canopy area per tree
parameters.relationship: Larger mature crowns raise canopy percentage but need more soil volume and edge clearance. Species presets drive the calculation; 50 m2 per tree is only an assumption behind UFS Figure 13, used for illustrative counts.

parameters.name: Soil volume and growing-medium depth
parameters.relationship: More continuous soil and depth support larger, longer-lived crowns, at a cost in parkade area (slab drops, notching, soil cells). The City requires adequate volumes, often above CSLA depths and set case by case (A.3.8).

parameters.name: Soil-limited crown credit
parameters.relationship: Counted crown = mature crown x min(1, soil available / soil required for its size class), so trees in thin or shared soil earn less canopy. The factor is a team assumption; no Vancouver growth model was found.

parameters.name: Planting level and soil continuity
parameters.relationship: Trees at grade in continuous soil are the City's priority (CDDG G4.5.1b) and R019 asks for continuous versus on-structure areas. Crowns on podium or terraces are reported separately; crowns under soffits or cantilevers earn no credit.

parameters.name: Underground setback
parameters.relationship: A wider underground setback frees continuous soil at grade for trees and infiltration but cuts parkade efficiency; draft CDDG allows variations if at least 0.9 m is kept and equivalent site area is provided.

parameters.name: Planted share of podium and roof
parameters.relationship: More planted podium and roof area raises vegetative cover and rainwater retention but adds irrigation demand and structural load; CDDG asks for trees and planting at podium and roof levels.

parameters.name: Site type A/B/C
parameters.relationship: Type C single-parcel sites target 10-15% canopy, Type A 20-25%, Type B 15-20%; R019 also has a 22% sentence for A and B, so classification changes the pass line.

metrics.name: Credited canopy at maturity, % of total site area
metrics.good: >= 10% (Type C band 10-15%; 15% or more exceeds the band)
metrics.basis: Force: rezoning_target. R019 targets table; RPSLD A.3.6 'should strive'. Block 11,468 m2 -> 1,147-1,720 m2. Credit uses soil-limited crowns and excludes soffit crowns; R019 asks for forecast at maturity.
metrics.method: Union of credited crown discs clipped to site / site area; existing canopy uses the greater of current or mature size

metrics.name: Canopy by level (grade continuous soil / podium on structure / tower terrace)
metrics.good: All three reported; grade canopy is the headline; no headline built from structure-only crowns
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. RPSLD A.4.1(g) asks separate calculations by cover type; CDDG G4.5.1(b) prioritises trees at grade; R019 1.2.3 splits continuous and on-structure area.
metrics.method: Group credited crown area by planting level and onStructure flag

metrics.name: Vegetative cover at maturity, % of site
metrics.good: Reference lines 30% (Type A total site) and 40% (Type B private parcel)
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. R019 gives no vegetative-cover target for Type C; the A and B values are shown only as editable reference lines.
metrics.method: Union(canopy, planted areas, green roofs) / site area

metrics.name: R019 Type A/B canopy: table band versus 22% sentence
metrics.good: Show both lines: table (A 20-25%, B 15-20%) and the 22% minimum sentence; a City planner resolves
metrics.basis: Force: rezoning_target. R019 1.2.1 says larger sites (Type A and B) should target a minimum 22% canopy; the 1.2.2 table gives B 15-20%. Internal inconsistency; Type C unaffected.
metrics.method: Preset toggle draws both lines

metrics.name: City-wide canopy context (not a parcel threshold)
metrics.good: 30% city-wide by 2050
metrics.basis: Force: city_aspiration. Park Board 7 Dec 2020; Urban Forest Strategy 2025; ODP policy 4.2.3. Downtown is among the three lowest-canopy neighbourhoods.
metrics.method: Reference line only

metrics.name: Regional canopy context (Metro 2050)
metrics.good: 40% regional canopy within the Urban Containment Boundary by 2050 (from 32%)
metrics.basis: Force: city_aspiration. Metro 2050 Action 3.2.1 as cited in the ODP regional table; UFS cites the Metro 2050 Nature and Ecosystems Roadmap 40% urban canopy target.
metrics.method: Reference line only, next to the 30% city line

metrics.name: Superseded city-wide canopy goal 22% by 2050
metrics.good: Do not use
metrics.basis: Force: city_aspiration. R019 text (July 2024) still quotes 22% city-wide; replaced by 30%. Kept visible and flagged.
metrics.method: Struck-through legend entry

metrics.name: Soil volume per tree, by size class
metrics.good: >= preset: large tree 30 m3 (Toronto EC 1.1); small and medium scaled to crown area (team)
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. TGS EC 1.1 gives 30 m3 per planting area (Tier 1). 30 m3 / 50 m2 = 0.6 m3 per m2 of crown is a team calculation. Vancouver sets the standard case by case (A.3.8).
metrics.method: Planting-area share x depth, per tree; compare with class preset; factor feeds crown credit

metrics.name: Illustrative tree count from 50 m2 per tree
metrics.good: Use only to size the illustration (about 23-34 trees); calculate with species crowns
metrics.bad: Treating 50 m2 as a City planning standard
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. UFS Figure 13 footnote assumes 50 m2 per tree for one figure; it is not a standard. The earlier spec called it the City's planning figure.
metrics.method: 1,147-1,720 m2 divided by 50 m2

modules.method: 1) Read planting polygons and tree points from Layer 0 (level, on-structure flag, soil depth). 2) For each tree take the species crown preset, draw a disc, clip to the site and remove parts under soffits or cantilevers. 3) Soil check: credit factor = min(1, soil available / soil required for its size class); scale the disc by it. 4) Union credited discs so overlaps are not double counted; canopy % = union area / site area (R019 plan view at maturity; adjacent City canopy in immediate proximity counted once). 5) Report canopy by level; grade canopy in continuous soil is the headline. 6) Vegetative cover = union(canopy, planted areas, green roofs) / site area. 7) Comparator mode gives a greening score for discussion only. Check: 11,468 m2 x 10% = 1,147 m2.
visualization: Plan view: credited canopy discs at maturity (solid) vs today (outline), crown credit shown by fill density, ground plane coloured by soil-depth class
Stacked bar of canopy by level (grade, podium, terrace) with the 10-15% Type C band, 30% city and 40% Metro lines, each with a source badge
Section strip showing soil depth and volume per tree, red where below the size-class preset
modules.human_judgment: Species choice and climate suitability, realism of crown growth in constrained soil, retention versus removal of existing trees, Indigenous plant knowledge and permissions, irrigation and maintenance, and the A/B/C classification (several towers under separate permits suggest Type B).
modules.limits: R019 canopy values are targets. Crowns are presets, not growth models; the soil-limited credit is a team rule. CSLA depth tables are paywalled and unopened. i-Tree and LiDAR give current, not future, canopy. Type C is an assumption.

modules.name: Greening at height (terraces, sky gardens, roofs)
modules.effort: M-L: about 7-9 person-days; blocked until CLIM sun-hours and wind outputs exist
modules.design_question: Can planting on podium terraces, sky gardens, facades and the tower roof survive and perform at height, and can trees and planters there be made safe, given sun, wind, irrigation, structure and glazing risk?
inputs: Layer0.Roofs/Terraces[] (Polygon3D + height + accessibility + program tag)
P05.Canopy planting polygons (M02)
CLIM: direct sun hours per surface; wind exposure ratio per terrace
STRC: slab live/dead load allowance and planter anchorage; SYST: maintenance access
P05.Rainwater supply (M04) and SPAC glazing adjacency
outputs: P05.HeightGreening {viability_class per patch, assembly type, runoff_reduction_pct, irrigation_deficit_mm, gate_checks[], lifesafety_checks[]}
Irrigation demand (m3/yr) to SYST and to P05-M04 water balance
Glazing-adjacent planting list to P05-M05
depends_on: STRC: structural load and anchorage preset

parameters.name: Height above grade and wind exposure
parameters.relationship: Wind exposure depends on height, nearby structures and funnelling; strong wind moves growing medium, limits species and adds uplift, so exposed terraces need windbreaks and wind-tolerant plants.

parameters.name: Growing-medium depth / assembly type
parameters.relationship: Extensive 60-150 mm is light, low-diversity and retains less; intensive 300 mm or more supports shrubs and small trees, retains more, weighs more and needs irrigation.

parameters.name: Plant water-use class
parameters.relationship: Low-water plants (Kc 0.3) cut annual runoff about 29% with a summer deficit of 54 mm; high-water plants (Kc 0.6) cut about 58% but the deficit exceeds 200 mm, raising irrigation and non-potable demand.

parameters.name: Roof accessibility and program
parameters.relationship: Non-accessible roofs should carry extensive green roof alongside solar or storage; accessible roofs favour common-use intensive green roof, so program tags drive assembly choice (RPSLD A.3.2).

parameters.name: Planting beside glass
parameters.relationship: Vegetation next to glazing raises collision risk unless glass is treated; Vancouver advises planting 0-1 m from glass; the Toronto comparator treats glazing 4 m above and 2.5 m to each side of rooftop vegetation.

parameters.name: Assembly dead and live load
parameters.relationship: Saturated weight rises with depth; the By-law requires loads per ASTM E2397, so deeper planting on towers competes with structure and tank space (see STRC packet).

parameters.name: Tree anchorage, falling objects and maintenance access
parameters.relationship: Wind-throw, lost growing medium, falling branches or pots over public space and gardener access decide whether planting at height is allowed at all; R019 asks for permanent cast-in-place roof planters, not containers.

metrics.name: Vegetated-roof code gates passed
metrics.good: All 5: wind resistance per CAN/CSA-A123.24; loads per ASTM E2397; waterproof roof; root barrier; retention and drainage layers
metrics.basis: Force: bylaw_requirement. VBBL 2025 Book I Art. 5.2.2.2(6) and 5.6.1.2(2); fire clause Art. 3.1.14.4 referenced.
metrics.method: Checklist with clause links

metrics.name: Life-safety gates cleared at height
metrics.good: All 5 signed off by a registered professional: tree anchorage for site wind; no trees on unrestrained exposed edges; falling-object zone over public realm; cast-in-place planters; safe gardener access
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. No Vancouver or Canadian standard found for tree anchorage at height; R019 1.1 asks for permanent cast-in-place roof planters and no container planting; City guide requires wind uplift and lateral load design.
metrics.method: Checklist with sign-off field linked to STRC and SYST

metrics.name: Annual rooftop runoff reduction
metrics.good: 29% (low-water plants) to 58% (high-water plants) at 150 mm medium
metrics.bad: Assuming more than 58% for a 150 mm roof
metrics.basis: Force: research_heuristic. Roehr and Kong (2010), modelled for Vancouver and reported by the City; not measured on towers.
metrics.method: Lookup by plant class; scale by area

metrics.name: Summer irrigation deficit
metrics.good: <= 8.6 mm (low-water plants with 50 mm retention tray)
metrics.basis: Force: research_heuristic. Roehr and Kong summary table; low-water plants without tray 54.4 mm.
metrics.method: Lookup; multiply by area for volume

metrics.name: Share of available roof area with green roof, PV or cool roof
metrics.good: 100% (comparator preset)
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. Toronto TGS v4 EC 2.3 is voluntary for applications from 2 June 2026 (page modified 24 Aug 2026), not Tier 1. Vancouver says non-accessible roofs 'should' include extensive green roof (RPSLD A.3.2).
metrics.method: Area share from roof tags

metrics.name: Viability thresholds (sun hours, wind exposure)
metrics.good: User-set per patch; no default until the CLIM wind study exists
metrics.bad: Default values shown as if sourced
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. No Vancouver numeric threshold for wind or sun at height; the City green roof guide is qualitative.
metrics.method: Editable dashed lines on the sun-wind scatter

modules.method: For each tagged terrace or roof patch read height, accessibility, sun hours and wind exposure from upstream modules. Pick an assembly from program (extensive 60-150 mm, semi-intensive, intensive 300 mm or more) and filter the City plant palette (about 95 plants, mostly native) by sun, wind and drought tolerance. Look up runoff reduction and irrigation deficit by plant water-use class (Roehr and Kong). Run the five code gates and the five life-safety gates (anchorage for site wind, edge restraint, falling-object zone, cast-in-place planters, gardener access); life-safety gates need registered-professional sign-off via STRC and SYST. Classify viability (viable / needs windbreak / not viable) with editable wind and sun thresholds, team assumptions because no sourced values were found. Flag glazing-adjacent patches for P05-M05.
visualization: Tower elevation with terrace and roof patches coloured by viability class (green / amber / red) and a legend
Scatter of sun-hours vs wind exposure per patch with dashed team-assumption threshold lines
Gate checklist (code gates and life-safety gates) with clause links, sign-off field and pass/fail badges
Bar chart of irrigation demand by patch against available non-potable supply
modules.human_judgment: Plant palette and ecological intent, tree anchorage and falling-object design by a registered professional, gardener access and safety, maintenance, whether a public terrace favours amenity over habitat, and Indigenous planting input.
modules.limits: No City numeric threshold for wind or sun at height; the Best Practices Guide is qualitative. Runoff and irrigation figures are modelled at 150 mm medium, not measured on towers. No standard found for tree anchorage at height. Facade greening has no City source found.

modules.name: Rainwater management (Building By-law detention, Rain City retention, reuse)
modules.design_question: How much on-site rainwater detention, release control and reuse does the block need under the Vancouver Building By-law, and how do green roofs, soil, tanks and groundwater limits change it?
inputs: Site.Boundary and net FSR
Layer0.Surfaces[] (roof, podium roof, green roof with depth and slope, paving, soft landscape, water) with areas
P05.Canopy landscaped areas (M02)
Optional SYST: non-potable demand (flushing, irrigation, cooling make-up); optional geotechnical depth to water table
outputs: P05.Rainwater {pathway, C_composite, V_required_m3, V_first_stage_m3, Qo_Ls, retention_mm, harvestable_m3_per_yr, groundwater_flag}
Tank volume and footprint to STRC / SYST (basement)
Water-balance table for rezoning submission (RPSLD D.3.1) and irrigation supply to P05-M03

parameters.name: Site area and net FSR
parameters.relationship: A site over 1,000 m2 or FSR over 1.0 follows the engineered pathway; maximum release scales at 25 L/s/ha, so a larger block may discharge more in total but still needs large absolute storage.

parameters.name: Composite runoff coefficient C
parameters.relationship: Roof and pavement (0.95) raise peak flow and detention; flat green roof 0.50 (>60-100 mm), 0.40 (>100-150), 0.30 (>150-250) and lawn 0.08-0.30 lower it; depths outside the table use the nearest band, flagged.

parameters.name: Landscaped and vegetated-roof area
parameters.relationship: The first-stage volume equals 15 mm x site area without landscaping; more ground landscaping or vegetated roof assembly shrinks that area and the first-stage volume.

parameters.name: Design storm
parameters.relationship: Intensity I = A x T^B (T in hours) from the 2100 IDF curve, 10-year return period (A 26.651, B -0.482); a longer duration lowers intensity but raises volume until V peaks.

parameters.name: Green-roof depth and plant class
parameters.relationship: Deeper medium lowers C and annual runoff by 29-58%; high-water plants raise retention but also irrigation, linking M04 to M03.

parameters.name: Underground setback and infiltration offset
parameters.relationship: Setbacks allow infiltration and trees; the draft CDDG notes a standard 5.0 m infiltration offset from foundations and asks that tanks stay out of setbacks where possible, trading parkade area against retention.

parameters.name: Non-potable reuse and its permit
parameters.relationship: Harvesting offsets potable use toward the required 20% indoor and 50% outdoor cuts, but needs an operating permit with two-monthly water-quality reporting; groundwater and perimeter drainage may not be harvested; detention credit for reuse storage is unstated.

parameters.name: Groundwater and infiltration limits
parameters.relationship: RPSLD E bars permanent groundwater discharge to City sewers and asks for hydrogeological and geotechnical studies; a deep basement near the water table limits sub-drains, tank depth and infiltration.

metrics.name: Compliance pathway
metrics.good: Engineered pathway (site > 1,000 m2 or FSR > 1.0); the block is 11,468 m2
metrics.bad: Treating the block as small-site (tank table)
metrics.basis: Force: bylaw_requirement. VBBL 2025 Table 2.4.2.5.-A; City page.
metrics.method: Rule lookup

metrics.name: Required detention volume V
metrics.good: Provided active storage >= V
metrics.basis: Force: bylaw_requirement. VBBL 2.4.2.5(5): Modified Rational Method, 10-year 2100 IDF, V maximised over D. Team illustration for this block: about 440 m3 at C 0.95, about 170 m3 at C 0.61. By-law example: 0.25 ha, C 0.75, tc 5 min -> 58.1 m3.
metrics.method: Iterate D (steps <= 15 min plus 60 min check); Qo = 25 L/s/ha x site area; tc = 5 min inlet time

metrics.name: Release rate, two stages
metrics.good: <= 5 for the first stage (15 mm x non-landscaped area); <= 25 thereafter; no orifice under 25 mm
metrics.basis: Force: bylaw_requirement. VBBL 2.4.2.5(6); Project Summary form lines 4-5 (permits opened from 1 Jan 2026).
metrics.method: Check outlet design against stage volumes

metrics.name: Retention depth vs Rain City 48 mm/day (reference only)
metrics.good: >= 48 mm retained (about 550 m3 for this block)
metrics.basis: Force: city_aspiration. Rain City Strategy private-property standard 'by 2022' is valid text; the City's GRI summary says private-property targets are superseded by Building By-law requirements. Kept as a stretch target.
metrics.method: Sum of retained depth x area / site area

metrics.name: Rain City 48 mm treated as binding on private sites
metrics.good: Do not use
metrics.bad: Presenting 48 mm as a compliance threshold
metrics.basis: Force: city_aspiration. The number is valid; the false claim was that it binds the project. Kept visible, struck through, with the FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag on bindingness only.
metrics.method: Struck-through legend entry

metrics.name: Potable water reduction (rezoning large developments)
metrics.good: >= 20% indoor and >= 50% outdoor, with a signed water balance
metrics.bad: Below either figure or no water balance
metrics.basis: Force: rezoning_policy_requirement. RPSLD March 2026 D.3.1-D.3.3; planted landscapes on structure included in outdoor demand; R019 outdoor baseline = 120 mm x landscaped area.
metrics.method: Baseline vs proposed water balance

metrics.name: No permanent groundwater discharge to City sewers
metrics.good: 0 from systems at or below the yearly high water table; hydrogeological study provided
metrics.bad: Any permanent sub-drain discharge to sewer
metrics.basis: Force: rezoning_policy_requirement. RPSLD E.3.1-E.3.2; temporary construction dewatering excepted. Site water-table depth is not modelled.
metrics.method: Flag basement depth against user-entered water-table level

metrics.name: City-wide capture target (context)
metrics.good: 90% captured and cleaned city-wide, long term
metrics.basis: Force: city_aspiration. Rain City Strategy aspirational target, not a site pass/fail.
metrics.method: Context line only

modules.method: Classify surfaces from Layer 0. Composite C = sum(C_i x A_i) / sum(A_i) from EDM Table 5-2 only (roof, pavement 0.95; flat green roof 0.50 for >60-100 mm, 0.40 for >100-150 mm, 0.30 for >150-250 mm); depths outside the table take the nearest band, flagged team assumption; Table 5-1 (CBD 0.95) is only the default before surfaces are tagged. For D = 5 to n min compute i = A x (D/60)^B, Qp = C x i x A_site / 3.6e6 m3/s, V = Qp x D - Qo x (D + tc) / 2 with Qo = 25 L/s/ha x site area, tc = 5 min; take the maximum. First-stage volume = 15 mm x (site area - landscaped - vegetated roof). Compare storage with V and the 5 and 25 L/s/ha limits. Unit test: By-law Note A-2.4.2.5.(5) returns 58.1 m3.
visualization: Hydrograph: uncontrolled inflow vs two-stage controlled outflow with shaded storage volume and the critical-duration marker
Plan false-colour of runoff coefficient by surface (0.30 green to 0.95 red)
Basement section with tank volume as a box, the depth-of-cover constraint and a water-table line
Badge row (pathway, V, first-stage volume, release rates, groundwater) each linked to the By-law or RPSLD clause

Rezoning approvals may carry site-specific conditions. Facade wind-driven rain, site groundwater levels and sea-level effects are not modelled.

modules.name: Bird-friendly glazing and night lighting
modules.design_question: How much glazing sits in the collision zone, how much is treated, which corner, fly-through and planting-behind-glass conditions remain, and how are night, obstruction and migration-season lighting controlled?
inputs: Layer0.Facade[] (Polygon3D + glazing flag + window-to-wall ratio from SPAC) and Layer 0 storey levels
Tree heights at maturity (M02), planted terraces and roofs (M02, M03), interior planted spaces (SPAC / program tags)
Treatment preset (pattern type and spacing) and lighting schedule (hours, CCT, shielding, obstruction-light type)
Distance to Stanley Park / habitat (M08)
outputs: P05.BirdRisk {zone_top_m, glazing_in_zone_m2, treated_pct, interior_planting_flags[], flags[], lighting_ok}
Treatment area and frit spec to SPAC (visible-light-transmission penalty to ENER daylight)
Annotated elevations for boards (PRES)
depends_on: SPAC: glazing ratio, interior planted spaces and facade materials

parameters.name: Risk-zone height
parameters.relationship: Vancouver's zone runs up to mature tree height or the fourth floor, whichever is highest, so tall podium storeys raise the zone and treated area; 12 m is only the Note's typical value, 16 m the Toronto and UBC comparator.

parameters.name: Marker spacing
parameters.relationship: Vancouver asks for gaps no greater than 5 cm vertically or 10 cm horizontally, on the exterior surface; UBC uses 5 x 5 cm and Toronto 50 x 50 mm. Tighter markers raise visibility but cut transparency and daylight.

parameters.name: Treated share of glazing in zone
parameters.relationship: Raising the treated share lowers collision probability; Vancouver gives no percentage; Toronto uses 85%; UBC tiers use 90%, 85% and 55%.

parameters.name: Glass corners and see-through passages
parameters.relationship: Glazed corners, railings and fly-through openings show sky or vegetation through the building; Vancouver asks to reduce clear passage; UBC treats corners 5 m each way and eliminates fly-through conditions.

parameters.name: Exterior planting adjacent to glass
parameters.relationship: Collisions are most acute at buildings near greenspace, so more planting needs more treatment; Vancouver advises planting 0-1 m from glass or treating it; Toronto adds 4 m above rooftop vegetation plus 2.5 m each side.

parameters.name: Interior planting behind glass
parameters.relationship: Enclosed sky gardens, winter gardens and atria show or reflect vegetation at any height; Vancouver says avoid interior landscaping near windows (3.3(c)(ii)). Glazing within distance d of interior planting joins the zone; d is a team assumption.

parameters.name: Facade, crown and feature lighting
parameters.relationship: Light spill attracts and disorients migrants; Vancouver asks for shielding, downlighting and no floodlighting; Toronto EC 5.4 turns rooftop and facade architectural lighting off 22:00-06:00 and limits unrated fixtures to 3,000 K.

parameters.name: Aviation obstruction lighting
parameters.relationship: A structure above 150 m needs Transport Canada Standard 621 marking and lighting; steady-burning red lights attract birds and a flashing-only option is described for towers, but its use on a building is unconfirmed.

parameters.name: Upper-floor interior light spill
parameters.relationship: Lit floorplates at 200-300 m can draw nocturnal migrants; automatic blinds or occupancy control after a set hour cut spill. Vancouver asks only to reduce unnecessary spill; the hour (23:00) is a team assumption.

parameters.name: Migration-season lights-out
parameters.relationship: Spring and autumn migration raises night collision risk; switching off non-essential crown, feature and interior lighting in those windows should lower it. Dates are a team assumption; Machtans cites an 83% drop at one Chicago site after lights-off.

metrics.name: Glazing treated within the risk zone
metrics.good: >= 85% (Toronto EC 5.1); 90% (UBC Tier 1, aligned with CSA A460-2019) as stretch
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. Vancouver sets no percentage. Toronto 85% read on its page; UBC tiers 90/85/55% read in the Backgrounder; CSA A460:19 not opened.
metrics.method: Treated glazing area / glazing area in zone

metrics.name: Marker gap compliance
metrics.good: Horizontal elements <= 5 cm apart vertically OR vertical elements <= 10 cm apart horizontally (dot patterns meet both), on the exterior surface
metrics.bad: Gaps above both limits, or markers on the interior surface
metrics.basis: Force: voluntary_guideline. Bird Friendly 3.3(a)(ii): 'no greater than 5 cm vertically or 10 cm horizontally'; use is 'encouraged'. Earlier spec said AND; corrected. Unit test: a 5 cm horizontal-stripe frit must pass.
metrics.method: Check pattern type and spacing against the OR rule

metrics.name: Untreated corner / fly-through / glass-railing conditions in zone
metrics.basis: Force: voluntary_guideline. Vancouver 3.3(a)(v) asks to reduce the appearance of clear passage; the zero count is stricter and follows UBC (fly-through eliminated, corners treated 5 m each way).
metrics.method: Corner detection and ray test between glazed faces

metrics.name: Untreated glazing near interior planting
metrics.basis: Force: voluntary_guideline. Vancouver 3.3(c)(ii) says avoid interior landscaping near windows; no source gives a distance, so d is a team assumption.
metrics.method: Buffer interior planted spaces by d; intersect with glazing at any height

metrics.name: Ventilation grate and open-pipe openings
metrics.good: <= 2 x 2 cm or <= 1 x 4 cm; open pipes capped
metrics.basis: Force: voluntary_guideline. Vancouver 3.3(e); Toronto EC 5.3 uses below 20 x 20 mm or 10 x 50 mm.
metrics.method: Schedule check

metrics.name: Night-lighting control (facade and roof)
metrics.good: Rooftop and facade architectural lighting downward and off 22:00-06:00; full-cutoff or Dark Sky fixtures, <= 3,000 K if unrated
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. Toronto EC 5.4 numbers read on its page; Vancouver guidance is qualitative (shield, downlight, no floodlights).
metrics.method: Schedule and fixture check

metrics.name: Obstruction lighting configuration
metrics.good: Marking and lighting to Standard 621 for above 150 m; written Transport Canada acceptance before assuming a flashing-only option
metrics.bad: Flashing-only assumed without acceptance, or the standard ignored
metrics.basis: Force: bylaw_requirement (binding federal regulation). Standard 621 s.5.4 describes a flashing-only configuration to cut bird fatalities for towers; building eligibility not confirmed; page read in part.
metrics.method: Select configuration; flag for Transport Canada review

metrics.name: Migration-season lights-out schedule
metrics.good: Non-essential crown, feature and interior lighting off through team-set spring and autumn windows
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. No Vancouver numeric source; windows are editable. Machtans cites an 83% drop in deaths at one Chicago site after night lights went off.
metrics.method: Schedule check

modules.method: Select glazed facade polygons. Zone top = max(top of 4th storey from Layer 0 levels, mature tree height at the facade); 12 m (Note) and 16 m (Toronto, UBC) are comparators. Add +4 m above each vegetated terrace or roof with a 2.5 m side buffer (Toronto). Add glazing within distance d of interior planting at any height. Clip glazed area to the zone and sum. Treated = markers meeting the OR rule on the exterior surface. Corner test: buffer glazed corners 5 m each way. Fly-through test: cast rays through paired glazed faces and railings. Report treated %, untreated area, flags and lighting checks. Example: a 448 m podium perimeter gives 448 x 12 = 5,376, x 16 = 7,168 or x 24 = 10,752 m2 in the zone before openings.
visualization: Unrolled facade elevations in false colour: red = untreated glazing in zone, amber = partly treated, green = treated, grey = opaque or outside zone, dashed line at the computed zone top
Terrace buffers and interior-planting buffers outlined; table of flagged corners, fly-through and interior-planting conditions
Pass/fail badges linked to clause text; 24-hour lighting schedule bar with migration windows and obstruction-light type
modules.human_judgment: Treatment product and its look, ornithologist review near habitat, trade-offs with views and daylight, lighting design intent, negotiation of obstruction lighting with Transport Canada, and whether to follow Vancouver's qualitative guidance or a stricter standard.
modules.limits: Vancouver guidance is voluntary and sets no percentage; CDDG and RPSLD A.4.1(e) require a response, not a number. CSA A460:19 unopened. Collision extent not locally assessed. Machtans' national 1% tall-building share is not a design threshold; per-building kills are highest. No reflectance model.

modules.name: Urban heat island and cool surfaces
modules.effort: M-L: about 5-7 person-days; needs the CLIM shadow module
modules.design_question: How much ground, podium and roof surface is shaded by vegetation, vegetated or reflective on a hot day, and does the scheme's own shadow cost public spaces their sun in cooler seasons?
inputs: Layer0.Surfaces[] with material tag (solar reflectance, thermal emittance and SRI presets from SPAC)
CLIM: hourly shade fraction per surface on a hot design day, split into vegetation and designed shade versus building shade
P05.Canopy credited crowns (M02) and green roofs (M03)
CLIM: fall-equinox new-shadow result on protected public spaces; Vancouver hot-day climate preset
outputs: P05.Heat {cooling_capacity_by_level (vegetation only), building_shade_reported, treated_hardscape_pct, roof_treated_pct, hot_cells[], sun_access_flag}
Surface temperature proxies to CLIM thermal-comfort module
Before/after maps for the boards

parameters.name: Surface solar reflectance and thermal emittance
parameters.relationship: Higher reflectance lowers surface temperature; stored separately because the cooling index uses reflectance (albedo) while SRI blends reflectance and emittance. Toronto uses aged SRI 64 (or reflectance 0.65, emittance 0.90) for low-slope roofs and SRI 29 for paving.

parameters.name: Vegetation and designed-shade fraction
parameters.relationship: In InVEST the shade term is tree canopy 2 m or taller, weighted 0.6 against 0.2 for albedo, so canopy and designed shade structures are the strongest lever; building shade is not in the index.

parameters.name: Building (tower) shade, reported not credited
parameters.relationship: The tower's shadow cools the plaza on hot days but removes sun in cool, overcast seasons; Solar Access Guidelines test new shadow on the fall equinox 10:00-16:00 PT, and the City lists greater shadowing as a harm of very tall buildings.

parameters.name: Evapotranspiration of green cover
parameters.relationship: Vegetation cools by evapotranspiration (index Kc x ETo / ETmax); trees can lower ambient air by 1-5 degrees C, but high-water plants need more irrigation.

parameters.name: Hardscape / impervious share
parameters.relationship: The hottest land surfaces in the June 2021 heat dome coincided with the highest impervious cover; more dark paving at grade and podium raises surface temperature.

parameters.name: Climate scenario
parameters.relationship: 2050s climate: average +2.4 degrees C and nine times as many days above 30 degrees C raise the baseline, so cooling measures matter more for later design years.

parameters.name: Residential versus non-residential frontage
parameters.relationship: Toronto sets 75% treated hardscape for residential uses and 50% for non-residential; a mixed-use tower needs the line chosen per frontage, so the pass line follows program tags.

metrics.name: Treated share of non-roof hardscape
metrics.good: >= 75% for residential frontage or >= 50% non-residential (SRI >= 29, shaded at solar noon on 21 June by 10-year canopy, or soft landscape >= 20% of lot)
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. Toronto TGS v4 EC 2.1 is voluntary for applications from 2 June 2026, not Tier 1; the earlier 50% used the non-residential value. Vancouver has no numeric rule found.
metrics.method: Treated area / non-roof hardscape area, by program tag

metrics.name: Roof area as green roof, PV or cool roof
metrics.good: 100% of available roof
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. Toronto EC 2.3 is voluntary since 2 June 2026; low-slope cool roof aged SRI 64 or initial reflectance >= 0.65 with emittance >= 0.90.
metrics.method: Roof area by treatment

metrics.name: Cooling capacity index CC (vegetation and designed shade only)
metrics.good: Proposal CC >= baseline CC at every level; hot-day index only
metrics.bad: Proposal CC below baseline, or raised only by building shade
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. InVEST factors method CC = 0.6 shade + 0.2 albedo + 0.2 ETI, where shade is tree canopy 2 m or taller. Earlier spec let tower shadow count; corrected. No pass line exists.
metrics.method: Per cell, area-weighted by level

metrics.name: New shadow on protected public spaces, fall equinox 10:00-16:00 PT (counter-metric)
metrics.good: 0 new shadow on listed parks and plazas
metrics.bad: Any new shadow without a rationale
metrics.basis: Force: rezoning_target. Solar Access Guidelines (Downtown Peninsula) 3.1.1: development 'should not cast new shadows' on listed parks; exceptions need public benefit and a detailed study. Computed in CLIM.
metrics.method: Read the CLIM fall-equinox shadow result

metrics.name: Hot-day land-surface-temperature classes (map legend)
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. Legend classes of the City's June 2021 heat-dome map; used for symbology only.
metrics.method: Colour ramp

modules.method: For each surface polygon read vegetation and designed-shade fraction (tree canopy 2 m or taller, pergolas), solar reflectance from the material preset and ETI = Kc x ETo / ETmax. Cooling capacity CC = 0.6 x shade + 0.2 x reflectance + 0.2 x ETI (InVEST factors method); building shade is excluded and reported separately as hot-day shade 12:00-17:00. Area-weight CC by level and compare with an untreated asphalt and concrete baseline. Pair CC with the CLIM fall-equinox new-shadow check (10:00-16:00 PT) so the trade-off shows. Treated hardscape follows Toronto EC 2.1 with the 75% or 50% line chosen by program tag, shade at solar noon on 21 June with 10-year crowns. Optional export to UMEP/SOLWEIG and pythermalcomfort for UTCI at pedestrian points.
visualization: False-colour plan for ground, podium and roof showing vegetation-only CC from 0 to 1 with a legend
Hot-day shade heat map 12:00-17:00 with vegetation shade and building shade drawn in separate layers
Proposal minus baseline difference map and bar by level, paired with the fall-equinox new-shadow map
Pass/fail chips for the Toronto-based treated-hardscape and roof checks, labelled voluntary since 2 June 2026
modules.human_judgment: Shade versus reflectance trade-offs (glare and reflected heat onto facades), plant choice, comfort and sun-access priorities for public spaces and vulnerable users, and reading CC as a relative hot-day index, not a temperature.
modules.limits: No Vancouver numeric heat-island requirement found; Toronto values are voluntary presets. CC is a hot-day index, not degrees C, and ignores winter sun. InVEST suits city-scale rasters: a block needs 1-2 m cells and its 2 ha green-area rule cannot trigger on 1.15 ha. Wind and night cooling are not modelled.

modules.name: Habitat and native planting
modules.effort: M: about 4-5 person-days (plant table curation dominates)
modules.design_question: How much layered, native, habitat-supporting planting and how many food assets does the scheme provide at ground, podium, roof and tower, and does it follow City habitat guidance and wildlife law?
inputs: P05.Canopy planting patches and trees (M02)
Plant palette table (species, native / culturally traditional flag, layer, pollinator or bird value, bloom period, water use, invasive flag)
Habitat feature tags (water, deadwood, perches, nesting, tower ledges and nest structures)
Lawn and artificial-turf areas; food-asset tags (garden, urban farm, edible landscaping)
outputs: P05.Habitat {layers_per_patch, native_share, lawn_share, features_per_patch, food_assets, bloom_species, patch_class}
Palette and water-use list to P05-M03 and M04
Habitat panel graphics for the boards

parameters.name: Vertical layers (ground, shrub, understorey, canopy)
parameters.relationship: More distinct foliage layers, up to six, raise bird and insect habitat value; Vancouver research found bird diversity rises with foliage height diversity.

parameters.name: Native and culturally traditional share
parameters.relationship: Higher native share supports local fauna and soil life; the City favours native and culturally traditional species, and the Toronto comparator asks at least 50% native at grade.

parameters.name: Lawn area
parameters.relationship: Less lawn means more habitat and less water, fertiliser and fuel; the guidelines say to minimise lawn and limit artificial turf to high-traffic uses.

parameters.name: Habitat features at grade
parameters.relationship: Snags, downed wood, water, logs, boulders and perches add refuge and food; the draft CDDG asks for them where a site is next to an ecological corridor, blue-green network or ESA.

parameters.name: Habitat features on the tower
parameters.relationship: Ledges, nest structures and roosts at height can serve peregrine falcons and swallows but invite gull and crow conflicts; BC Wildlife Act s.34 protects peregrine nests at all times, so each feature needs a management note.

parameters.name: Food assets
parameters.relationship: RPSLD B.3.1 requires at least three food assets (R019 lists gardens, urban farm, edible landscaping); they compete with habitat planting for terrace and roof area and add maintenance and access needs.

parameters.name: Bloom continuity
parameters.relationship: At least two native flowering species with continuous bloom (Toronto EC 2.2 comparator) feed pollinators across seasons; fewer species leave seasonal gaps. No Vancouver numeric source.

parameters.name: Nesting-season timing and wildlife law
parameters.relationship: Planting, clearing and roof works during nesting can harm nests; the Bird Friendly guidelines tell users to comply with the BC Wildlife Act and Migratory Birds Convention Act, so work windows need a qualified professional.

parameters.name: Contiguity and patch size
parameters.relationship: Larger contiguous patches hold more species; City habitat types need 3-8.5 ha (forest) or 0.5-3 ha (shrub), far above a 1.15 ha block, so the site acts as a stepping stone.

metrics.name: Layers present in the main contiguous patch
metrics.good: 4 (ground, shrub, understorey, canopy)
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. Layers are named in Vancouver guidance; the count threshold is the team's reading.
metrics.method: Palette layer attribute per patch

metrics.name: Native share of planted area
metrics.good: >= 50% in each of trees, shrubs, herbaceous (at-grade landscape)
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. Toronto TGS v4 EC 2.2 is voluntary for applications from 2 June 2026, not Tier 1; Vancouver gives no percentage but favours native and culturally traditional species.
metrics.method: Area-weighted species flags

metrics.name: Lawn share of planted area
metrics.good: <= 10% (editable preset)
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. Guidelines say 'minimize lawn' without a number.
metrics.method: Area share

metrics.name: Food assets delivered
metrics.basis: Force: rezoning_policy_requirement. RPSLD B.3.1 minimum three food assets; R019 section 2 lists options and edible-landscaping duties (signage, accessible to residents or public).
metrics.method: Count tagged assets; check signage and access

metrics.name: Native flowering species with continuous bloom
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. Toronto EC 2.2 (voluntary since 2 June 2026); no Vancouver number.
metrics.method: Palette bloom-period attribute

metrics.name: Tower habitat features with management note
metrics.good: Each feature tagged with species intent and a gull and crow management note
metrics.bad: Features with no note, or none considered
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. No City numeric source; context from Wildlife Act s.34 (peregrine nests protected) and the Bird Strategy (Barn Swallow decline).
metrics.method: Feature tags and note field

metrics.name: Biodiversity units vs baseline (optional comparator)
metrics.good: Net gain of at least 10% (England's rule; not applicable in Vancouver)
metrics.basis: Force: comparator_other_jurisdiction. England's statutory metric uses size, quality, location and type; shown only as a method example.
metrics.method: Area x distinctiveness x condition x strategic significance (inputs not opened)

modules.method: Join the plant palette to planting polygons. For each contiguous patch (Shapely union of adjacent polygons) compute layers present, native share by area, lawn and turf share, habitat feature counts and invasive-species flags. Compare patch area with City habitat-type minimum areas to label it stepping stone or core (a block is a stepping stone). Count food assets (RPSLD B.3.1), native flowering species with continuous bloom, and tower habitat features with a gull and crow management note. Check works timing against nesting windows and wildlife law. Use the City green-roof plant list (about 95 plants, mostly native) as default palette and let teams add Host Nation guidance. Optionally compute a BNG-style unit score for discussion.
visualization: Plan: patches coloured by layer completeness (0-4), hatched where non-native dominates
Stacked bars of species by layer, bloom-period strip by month, and a section diagram showing layers on podium and roof
Habitat feature and food-asset checklist with icons and counts, tower features marked with their management note
modules.human_judgment: Which species are culturally traditional and appropriate (Host Nations' knowledge and permission), ecological intent, maintenance regime, wildlife conflicts (gulls and crows on roofs, window strikes, nesting law), food-asset programming, and amenity versus habitat priorities.
modules.limits: Native lists should come from the City green-roof guide appendix and Host Nation guidance. A 1.15 ha block cannot meet City habitat-type minimum areas. Vancouver has adopted no biodiversity index. The Re-Wilding Action Plan was not opened. Survival at height depends on M03.

modules.name: Ecological connectivity and access to nature
modules.effort: M-L: about 5-7 person-days (a distance-only v1-lite is about 2 days)
modules.design_question: How well does the block link to Stanley Park, the water and the mountains ecologically and visually, and who can reach nature within walking distance of it?
inputs: Site geolocation and polygon (SITE)
City Open Data: parks polygons, greenways, public trees
ODP Map 7 Ecological Network vision (image; corridors digitised by the team)
P05.Canopy and P05.Habitat patches (M02, M07)
SITE: public-views module for protected mountain and water views and QE Park view cone; program tags (residential, office floors)
outputs: P05.Connectivity {distance_to_core_m, stepping_stones[], corridor_frontage_m, trees_in_view_per_floor_band[], nature_within_walk, views_kept}
Link graph for the boards
Inputs to P05-M05 (habitat adjacency) and P05-M01 (L2.3.1 half b)

parameters.name: Distance to nearest core and stepping-stone habitat
parameters.relationship: Shorter distance and continuous tree or planted links along streets and greenways improve connectivity; the City treats Stanley Park as a core and smaller natural areas as stepping stones.

parameters.name: Frontage on an ecological corridor or greenway
parameters.relationship: A frontage on an opportunity corridor lets site planting extend it; corridor alignments are conceptual and follow blue-green and greenway routes.

parameters.name: Publicly accessible planted area
parameters.relationship: Counted natural spaces in the City's metric are larger than 0.5 ha, so a block contributes only if a contiguous accessible patch reaches that size; smaller patches act as stepping stones.

parameters.name: Trees visible from dwellings and workplaces
parameters.relationship: More mature trees within view raise the count; above about 10-15 storeys (team estimate) only terraces and sky gardens can supply trees, so the test counts crowns of at least 25 m2 within 30 m, per floor band.

parameters.name: Distance basis (straight-line versus network)
parameters.relationship: Straight-line distance is shorter than the walking route, so a pass on one can fail on the other; both are computed and the network result is shown for the residential program only.

parameters.name: View framing to mountains and water
parameters.relationship: Tower position and orientation set which protected views and public spaces keep mountain and water visibility; the SITE views module computes it and M08 passes it to M01 as L2.3.1 half (b).

metrics.name: Distance to public green space of at least 1 ha (residential program)
metrics.good: <= 300 m (network distance shown; straight-line also reported)
metrics.basis: Force: research_heuristic. 3-30-300 rule citing WHO 2017 (green space of at least 1 ha within 300 m, about 5 minutes); designed for homes, not offices or hotels.
metrics.method: Network and straight-line distance to parks polygons with area_hectare >= 1; residential tags only

metrics.name: Natural space larger than 0.5 ha within a 5-minute walk
metrics.good: Yes, within about 400 m (4.8 km/h x 5 min, editable)
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. Biodiversity Strategy tracks this metric by neighbourhood without a pass line; the 400 m conversion is the team's.
metrics.method: Distance to natural-area polygons

metrics.name: Mature trees in view per floor band
metrics.good: >= 3 crowns of at least 25 m2 within a 30 m buffer, reported per floor band
metrics.basis: Force: research_heuristic. Konijnendijk says the number 3 lacks scientific support, gives no viewing distance and ignores upper floors; 25 m2 and 30 m are an unpublished Dutch method example. Earlier spec marked it verified.
metrics.method: Count qualifying crowns in the buffer per floor band; terraces and sky gardens counted from M02 and M03

metrics.name: Frontage on ODP opportunity corridor or City greenway
metrics.good: Any frontage used to extend the corridor with trees and planting
metrics.bad: Frontage present but planting breaks the link
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. Corridor map is conceptual and image-only; greenways dataset is available.
metrics.method: Overlay frontage with greenways and digitised corridors

metrics.name: Protected-view result passed to M01
metrics.good: SITE reports each mountain-ridgeline and water view and the QE Park view cone as kept or blocked, with source
metrics.basis: Force: team_assumption. Passes the SITE result to M01 as L2.3.1 half (b); Public Views Guidelines (10 Jul 2024) and CDDG 4.10 govern but were not opened in full.
metrics.method: Read the SITE views output

modules.method: Compute straight-line and street-network distance from the site edges to (a) the Stanley Park polygon as core and (b) parks over 0.5 ha as stepping stones, using the City parks dataset. Overlay frontages on the greenways layer and on corridors digitised from ODP Map 7. Run the trees-in-view heuristic per floor band: sample window points on each tagged floor plate and count crowns of at least 25 m2 within the 30 m buffer (M02, public-trees data), terraces included. Build a link graph (core, stepping stones, corridors, site patches) and report the shortest continuous green link. Read mountain and water views from the SITE views module and pass them to M01. v1-lite is distance and frontage only.
visualization: Context map (about 1.5 km) with Stanley Park, parks, greenways, ODP corridors and site; labelled distance lines; note that the site north arrow is rotated from the street grid
Link-graph overlay on the map
Trees-in-view count per floor band as a heat strip beside the tower elevation, with the above-10-15-storey caveat marked
modules.human_judgment: Whether proposed links are real ecological connections for species or symbolic, the cultural meaning of Stanley Park, the water and the mountains, Indigenous naming and relationships, view-corridor trade-offs, and long-term stewardship.
modules.limits: ODP Map 7 corridors are conceptual and not a dataset (open-data catalogue returned no ecological-network layer). 3-30-300 targets neighbourhoods and homes, not supertall floors. The City gives no stepping-stone distance threshold. Views depend on the SITE views module.
