sources.extract: Cores are large natural areas such as Stanley Park; stepping stones such as Renfrew Ravine; corridors are linear park-like streets; corridor locations are general areas of opportunity; ESA identification adds no new regulation.

sources.title: Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments (amended 31 March 2026)
sources.extract: Large development = 8,000 m2 or 45,000 m2 floor area (block qualifies). A.3.1 park dedication case by case; A.3.6 canopy 'should strive'; A.3.8 soil per CSLA, often exceeded; A.4.1(e) Re-Wilding; B.3.1 three food assets; D.3.2-3.3 water -20%/-50%; E.3.1 no groundwater to sewer.

sources.title: Sustainable Large Developments Admin Bulletin (R019), last amended 12 July 2024
sources.extract: Type C = single parcel over excavated parkade, occasionally under Higher Buildings Policy. Canopy A 20-25%, B 15-20%, C 10-15%; cover A 30%, B 40%; at maturity, plan view. Quotes 22% city-wide and 22% for A/B sites; roof planters cast in place; 1.2.3 soil split.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy (amended through 31 March 2026)
sources.extract: Design excellence, community benefits, energy/GHG (or Passive House); applies to buildings entering the Queen Elizabeth Park or other view corridors; no ecology, bird or rainwater clause; Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings applies. The VTC-brief URL now returns this text.

sources.title: Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings (last amended 27 November 2024)
sources.extract: Embodied carbon design report, resilient buildings worksheet, enhanced commissioning, sub-metering; no rainwater, bird or ecology requirement in this version.

sources.title: City-wide Design and Development Guidelines, Council report RTS 18459 with Appendix A (draft), 28 July 2026
sources.extract: S4.5.1 meet or exceed CSLA soil depths; G4.5.1 prioritise trees at grade, plant podium and roof; G4.5.2-4.5.7 layered planting, habitat; 4.8 Bird Friendly; 4.9 solar access; 4.10 public views; S1.7.1 setback 0.9 m; G1.7.3 tanks; tower roofs green.

sources.title: City-wide Design and Development Guidelines (City page)
sources.extract: Council approved 28 July 2026; takes effect 27 October 2026; applies to most conditional development permit and rezoning applications; final guidelines to be posted (only the council report linked on 21 Oct 2026).

sources.title: Vancouver Building By-law 2025, Book II insert pages (Art. 2.4.2.5 Rainwater Management and Notes)
sources.extract: 2.4.2.5 engineered pathway: detention by Modified Rational Method, 10-year 2100 IDF; 5 then 25 L/s/ha; orifice >= 25 mm; example 58.1 m3. Rainwater systems need an operating permit and two-monthly water-quality reporting; 2.7.1.2 bars harvesting groundwater.

sources.title: Rainwater management on private property (City page)
sources.extract: Engineered pathway for sites over 1,000 m2 or FSR over 1.0; permits opened after 1 Jan 2026 follow By-law 14343 as amended by 14488; rezoning-policy rainwater requirements simplified July 2023 and removed from Zoning and Development By-law 1 Jan 2024; site-specific conditions may continue.

sources.title: Engineering Design Manual, Section 5.2 amendment (11 February 2025)
sources.extract: Table 5-1 CBD C 0.95 (whole-development); Table 5-2 roofs, pavement 0.95; flat green roof 0.30 (>150-250 mm), 0.40 (>100-150), 0.50 (>60-100); lawns 0.08-0.30; 2100 IDF 10-year A 26.651, B -0.482; inlet time 5 min.

sources.title: Rainwater Management Project Summary form (permits opened in 2026)
sources.extract: Engineered pathway form: first-stage capacity 15 mm x site area without landscaping; release <= 5 L/s/ha first stage, <= 25 L/s/ha second; sealed calculations and Schedule B.

sources.title: Rain City Strategy
sources.extract: Capture and clean 90% of average annual rainfall; manage runoff from 40% of impervious area by 2050; design standard 48 mm (public Nov 2019, private by 2022). About 70% of rainfall arrives on days under 24 mm; 1,200-1,600 mm per year.

sources.title: Green rainwater infrastructure policies and reports (City page)
sources.extract: Target: capture and clean 90% of rainwater; performance standard 48 mm per day; lists Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings, RPSLD and Groundwater bulletins.

sources.title: GRI Pathways Study - Summary Sheet
sources.extract: States Rain City performance targets (24 and 48 mm/day) are superseded on private property by Building By-law requirements; high-rise non-residential with full-site parkade has no landscape-based pathway at 48 mm.

sources.title: Green roofs (City page)
sources.extract: Extensive medium usually 150 mm or less; intensive 300-900 mm or more; semi-intensive 60-900 mm; layers; co-benefits; cites Roehr and Kong runoff reduction 29% and 58%.

sources.title: Green roofs with low and high water use plants: runoff and irrigation summary table (Roehr and Kong 2010)
sources.publisher: City of Vancouver (citing Canadian Water Resources Journal 35(1))
sources.extract: Traditional roof runoff 2,578 m3/ha/yr; low-water plants (Kc 0.3) cut 29%, summer deficit 54.4 mm (8.6 mm with 50 mm tray); high-water plants (Kc 0.6) cut 58%, deficit over 200 mm.

sources.title: Rain City Green Roof Best Practices Guide
sources.extract: Wind exposure rises with height; windbreaks; roofs must resist wind uplift and lateral pressure (ANSI/SPRI, NRCC); extensive 60-150 mm, intensive over 300 mm; about 95 recommended plants; qualitative only on wind and sun.

sources.title: Vancouver Building By-law 2025, Book I (Volume 1)
sources.extract: Art. 5.2.2.2(6): wind resistance of vegetated roof assemblies per CAN/CSA-A123.24. Art. 5.6.1.2(2): vegetated roof permitted if it meets Art. 3.1.14.4, loads per ASTM E2397, waterproof roof, root barrier, retention and drainage layers.

sources.title: Bird Friendly Design Guidelines - Considerations for Development Permit (adopted Jan 2015, amended 16 May 2017)
sources.extract: Use 'encouraged'. 3.3(a)(i) zone to mature tree height or 4th floor; (ii) exterior markers, gaps no greater than 5 cm vertically or 10 cm horizontally; (c) plant 0-1 m from glass, avoid interior landscaping near windows; (d) shield, downlight; (e) grates 2x2 or 1x4 cm; BC Wildlife Act and MBCA note.

sources.title: Bird Friendly Design Guidelines: Explanatory Note (January 2015)
sources.extract: 4th floor is about 12 m; high-rise offices with reflective glass near natural areas can cause disproportionate collisions; local collision extent not scientifically assessed; habitat table (forest 3-8.5 ha, shrub 0.5-3 ha) and up to six foliage layers.

sources.title: Vancouver Bird Strategy (January 2015, updated December 2020)
sources.publisher: Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation
sources.extract: Cover: 'January 2015 (Updated December 2020)'. 16-42 million birds collide with glass in Canada yearly; a 2017 study found the problem acute near greenspace; Barn Swallows down over 90% on the Pacific coast; names Rewilding Action Plan (2014).

sources.title: Biodiversity Strategy
sources.publisher: Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation
sources.extract: Goal: increase amount and ecological quality of natural areas. Target: restore or enhance 25 ha by 2020. Metric: percent of residents within a 5-minute walk of natural spaces over 0.5 ha. Green roofs recognised as urban habitat.

sources.title: 2025 Urban Forest Strategy
sources.extract: 30% canopy by 2050 (Park Board 7 Dec 2020); 25% in 2022; Downtown among lowest; Figure 13 footnote assumes 50 m2 per tree; Metro 2050 roadmap 40% urban canopy; trees cool 1-5 degrees C; June 2021 land-surface-temperature classes.

sources.title: Climate Change Adaptation Strategy 2024-2025 Update and Action Plan
sources.extract: 2050s: about 2.4 degrees C warmer; three times as many days above 25 degrees C and nine times as many above 30; summer rainfall about -4%; one-day extreme rainfall +20% to 86 mm.

sources.title: Blue green systems (City page)
sources.extract: Networks of connected park-like streets managing water and land; Rain City objectives incl. heat island mitigation; Typology Study with 9 types; designed for 1-in-10-year storms.

sources.title: Open Data: Public trees
sources.publisher: City of Vancouver Open Data Portal
sources.extract: 184,268 records with species, height_m, diameter_cm, geometry; Open Government Licence - Vancouver; modified 19 Oct 2026 (read via the portal API metadata).

sources.title: Open Data: Parks - polygon representation
sources.publisher: City of Vancouver Open Data Portal
sources.extract: 254 park polygons with area_hectare and classification; Open Government Licence - Vancouver.

sources.title: Open Data: LiDAR 2022 and Greenways
sources.publisher: City of Vancouver Open Data Portal
sources.extract: LiDAR 2022 LAS tiles over 134 km2; Greenways dataset (24 records, updated weekly); catalogue search found no canopy raster, ecological-network or GRI layer.

sources.title: Machtans, Wedeles and Bayne (2013) Incidence of bird collisions with buildings, Canada
sources.extract: About 25 million (16-42 million) birds a year; houses about 90%, low-rise under 10%, tall buildings about 1% but highest per-structure kill rates; mitigation at few buildings helps; cites 83% drop at a Chicago site after lights off.

sources.title: UBC Bird Backgrounder (Campus and Community Planning)
sources.extract: Tiers 1/2/3 treat 90%/85%/55% of glazing up to 16 m or 4 m above tallest vegetation, plus glazing next to habitat; Tier 1 aligned with CSA; frit <= 5 x 5 cm; corners 5 m each way; grates 20x20 or 40x10 mm. Text read in browser.

sources.title: CSA A460:19 Bird-friendly building design (standard)
sources.publisher: CSA Group / Standards Council of Canada
sources.extract: Not opened; content known only through UBC and FLAP Canada summaries.

sources.title: Toronto Green Standard v4 (interim): Ecology and Biodiversity, mid-to-high-rise
sources.extract: EC 1.1 30 m3 per planting area (Tier 1). EC 2.1 residential 75%, non-residential 50%; EC 2.2 50% native, two continuous-bloom natives; EC 2.3 100% roof: EC 2.1-2.3 voluntary from 2 June 2026. EC 5.1-5.4 bird items (85%, 16 m, 50 mm, off 22:00-06:00, 3,000 K); page modified 24 Aug 2026.

sources.title: Toronto Green Standard v4 (interim): Water Quality and Efficiency
sources.extract: WQ 1.1 retain 50% of annual rainfall, about 5 mm per event; WQ 1.3 green roof 80% of available roof; Tier 2 irrigation potable reduction 60%. Retention-based comparator very different from Vancouver detention. Voluntary status not re-checked.

sources.title: Konijnendijk (2023) Evidence-based guidelines for greener, healthier, more resilient neighbourhoods: the 3-30-300 rule (Europe PMC full text)
sources.extract: 3 trees in view: the number is not supported by scientific evidence; no viewing distance; no upper floors. 30% canopy per neighbourhood. 300 m to green space of at least 1 ha (WHO 2017). Dutch example: 25 m2 canopy, 30 m buffer.

sources.title: Understanding biodiversity net gain (UK Government guidance)
sources.extract: Developers must deliver 10% net gain; units depend on size, quality, location and type; habitats maintained 30 years; developments of 0.2 ha or less exempt from 6 Aug 2026. Not Vancouver law.

sources.title: London Plan Policy G5 Urban Greening (Urban Greening Factor)
sources.extract: Not opened: the site returned a bot challenge, which was not bypassed. Recalled, unverified: target scores 0.4 residential and 0.3 commercial.

sources.title: InVEST User Guide: Urban Cooling Model
sources.extract: CC = 0.6 shade + 0.2 albedo + 0.2 ETI; shade = proportion covered by tree canopy 2 m or taller (building shade not included); ETI = Kc x ETo / ETmax; 2 ha green-area rule; cooling distance 450 m; intensity method for night.

sources.title: Using Green Roofs to Reduce Heat Islands (US EPA)
sources.extract: Green-roof surfaces can be 56 degrees F cooler; runoff reduction 60-100% (extensive to intensive, event-based). Not comparable with Vancouver's modelled annual 29-58%; context only.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy Review: public engagement exhibit
sources.extract: p.6 'A City in Nature' cites ODP policy L2.3.1: buildings and sites provide space for nature; protect views and connections to mountains, water, landscapes. p.4, p.11 wind and shadowing; p.9 QE Park view cone. Feeds the competition brief; options early 2027.

sources.title: Solar Access Guidelines for the Downtown Peninsula (approved 17 Sept 2025, amended 29 July 2026)
sources.extract: 3.1.1 development should not cast new shadows on listed parks on the fall equinox 10:00-16:00 PT; exceptions need public benefit and a detailed study; tree and shade-structure shadows are excluded from the existing baseline.

sources.title: Transport Canada Standard 621 - Obstacle Marking and Lighting (CARs)
sources.extract: Marking always required above 150 m AGL. Red configuration uses flashing CL-864 and steady CL-810. s.5.4 Configuration A' (flashing-only, to reduce bird fatalities because steady lights attract birds) is for towers and skeletal structures. First 200,000 of 233,211 characters read.

sources.title: Migratory Birds Convention Act, 1994 (S.C. 1994, c. 22)
sources.extract: s.5 bars possession and trade of migratory birds and nests without authorization; s.13 offences; nest rules sit in the regulations (s.12). Current to 2026-09-30. First 100,000 characters read.

sources.title: Migratory Birds Regulations, 2022 (SOR/2022-105)
sources.extract: s.5(1)(c) bars damaging, destroying, removing or disturbing a nest without authorization; s.5(1)(b) eggs; s.5(2) conditions for nests without live birds or viable eggs; Schedule 1 species have notice periods. First 100,000 characters read.

sources.title: Wildlife Act (BC), s.34 Wildlife protection
sources.extract: s.34 protects birds and eggs; nests of eagle, peregrine falcon, gyrfalcon, osprey, heron and burrowing owl are protected at all times; other birds' nests protected while occupied. First 100,000 characters read.

sources.title: Integrated Stormwater Management Best Practice Toolkit, Volume II (Citywide Integrated Rainwater Management Plan, March 2016, marked FINAL DRAFT)
sources.extract: Absorbent landscapes: growing medium at least 300 mm for lawn to store 60 mm rain; organic matter 8% lawn, 15% beds; rain garden 450 mm minimum; tree well soil cells described without per-tree volumes.

sources.title: Public views (City page; Public Views Guidelines approved 10 July 2024)
sources.extract: 10 July 2024 Council replaced the View Protection Guidelines with Public Views Guidelines; views of the North Shore Mountains remind us of our connection to nature; QE Park view among protected views. Guidelines PDF not opened.

sources.title: Rewilding Vancouver Action Plan (2014), named in RPSLD A.4.1(e), the Bird Strategy and the Green Roof Guide
sources.extract: Not opened and URL not located; the link points to the Bird Strategy, which names the plan. Content unknown; RPSLD asks for a response to the Re-Wilding Strategy.

flags.claim: Rainwater requirements for the tower come through rezoning policy and the Rain City 48 mm/day standard binds private sites.
flags.correction: Rainwater rules were simplified in the rezoning policies in July 2023 and removed from the Zoning and Development By-law on 1 Jan 2024. The Vancouver Building By-law 2025, Book II Art. 2.4.2.5 now governs: engineered pathway for sites over 1,000 m2, detention with 10-year 2100 IDF, release 5 then 25 L/s/ha. The City says Rain City 48 mm targets are superseded on private property; they remain an aspiration. Site-specific rezoning conditions may still apply.
flags.detail: Sources P05-S10, P05-S11, P05-S16, P05-S07. Governing text for permits opened after 1 Jan 2026 is By-law 14343 as amended by 14488. In r1 the 48 mm number is kept as a valid city_aspiration; only the bindingness claim is struck through.

flags.claim: The city-wide canopy target is 22% by 2050.
flags.correction: 30% by 2050 (Park Board 7 Dec 2020; Urban Forest Strategy 2025; ODP policy 4.2.3).
flags.detail: The R019 bulletin text (July 2024) still quotes 22%; its Type C site target of 10-15% canopy is separate and still stands. Sources P05-S05, P05-S25, P05-S01.

flags.claim: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy linked in the VTC brief is the governing text and sets ecology or City in Nature criteria.
flags.correction: The same URL now returns the policy amended through 31 March 2026. It sets design excellence, community benefit and energy/GHG (or Passive House) requirements and has no ecology, bird or rainwater clause; the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings applies.
flags.detail: Ecology obligations for a block this size come from the ODP (adopted 31 March 2026), the Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments and R019, and the CDDG (effective 27 Oct 2026). The City in Nature framing sits in the engagement exhibit (see r1 flag). Sources P05-S06, P05-S04, P05-S05, P05-S09, P05-S41.

flags.claim: 'City in Nature' has no official definition: the phrase is not in official text and the nearest framing is ODP Big Idea 3 plus Part 5 s.4 Ecology.
flags.correction: The City's Higher Buildings Policy Review exhibit (named in the VTC brief) has a section 'A City in Nature' citing ODP policy L2.3.1 ('City in nature, nature in the city'): buildings and sites provide space for nature, and views and connections to mountains, water and landscapes are protected. M01 now has two halves: space for nature (M02-M07) and views (SITE, M08).
flags.detail: Read in full (48 pp) on 21 Oct 2026; links to Public Views and the QE Park view cone. L2.3.1 not found in the adopted ODP plain text (235 pp) or draft ODP (104 pp; FG-numbered policies only), so clause location is unverified. Sources P05-S41, P05-S01, P05-S48.

flags.claim: Vancouver Bird Friendly Design Guidelines require marker gaps <= 5 cm vertical AND <= 10 cm horizontal (P05-M05 metric, status verified).
flags.correction: Clause 3.3(a)(ii) says 'no greater than 5 cm vertically or 10 cm horizontally', markers on the exterior surface; use is 'encouraged', not required. M05 now passes a pattern meeting either limit (dots meet both); unit test: a 5 cm horizontal-stripe frit passes.
flags.detail: Read in the City PDF (May 2017 amendment) on 21 Oct 2026. Source P05-S21.

flags.claim: 'At least 3 mature trees visible from each dwelling or workplace' is a verified threshold (P05-M08).
flags.correction: The paper says the number 3 is not supported by scientific evidence, sets no viewing distance and ignores upper floors. M08 treats it as a research_heuristic with the paper's Dutch example (crowns of at least 25 m2 within a 30 m buffer), reported per floor band.
flags.detail: Konijnendijk 2023, Europe PMC full text. Not Vancouver policy. Above about 10-15 storeys only terraces and sky gardens can satisfy it (team estimate). Source P05-S36.

flags.claim: Toronto Green Standard v4 EC 2.1, EC 2.2 and EC 2.3 are current Toronto Tier 1 requirements, and EC 2.1 is 50% for a mixed-use tower.
flags.correction: Toronto's page marks EC 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 voluntary for applications submitted on or after 2 June 2026 (page modified 24 Aug 2026). EC 2.1 is 75% for residential uses and 50% for non-residential; M06 now chooses the line per frontage.
flags.detail: EC 1.1 (30 m3), EC 5.1-5.4 show no voluntary note. Re-check before use. Source P05-S34.

flags.claim: 50 m2 of canopy per tree is the City's own planning figure.
flags.correction: It is a footnote assumption for UFS Figure 13 ('Assumes 50 m2 of canopy per tree'), not a standard. Calculations use species crowns; 50 m2 only sizes the illustrative tree count.
flags.detail: Source P05-S25.

flags.claim: R019 quotes 22% only as the outdated city-wide canopy goal.
flags.correction: R019 1.2.1 also says larger sites (Type A and B) should target a minimum 22% canopy, which conflicts with its own Type B band of 15-20%. M02 shows both for Type A/B and flags the inconsistency; Type C (10-15%) is unaffected.

flags.claim: The Vancouver Bird Strategy is a 2015 document.
flags.correction: The cover reads 'January 2015 (Updated December 2020)'; cite it as 2020 (update). The 2017 study it cites appears only in the update.
flags.detail: Source P05-S23.

flags.claim: A 'verified' status means a threshold binds the project.
flags.correction: Status now records only whether the source says it. A required force field (bylaw_requirement, rezoning_policy_requirement, rezoning_target, voluntary_guideline, city_aspiration, comparator_other_jurisdiction, research_heuristic, team_assumption) records bindingness; M01 pass/fail counts only the first two.
flags.detail: Without it, 3-30-300, Roehr and Kong values, 'should strive' targets and voluntary guidelines read like by-law items. Sources P05-S04, P05-S10, P05-S21, P05-S36.

flags.claim: The InVEST cooling shade term can include the tower's own shadow, so shading by the tower raises cooling capacity.
flags.correction: InVEST defines shade as tree canopy 2 m or taller; building shade is not in the index. M06 credits only vegetation and designed shade, reports building shade separately, and pairs CC with the fall-equinox new-shadow check.
flags.detail: The earlier spec read shade as 'by the tower or by trees', which would reward overshadowing public space. Solar Access Guidelines also exclude tree shadows from the shadow baseline. Sources P05-S39, P05-S42, P05-S41.

flags.claim: The bird-collision zone top is 12 m (4th floor, Explanatory Note).
flags.correction: Vancouver's clause says up to the fourth floor or mature tree height, whichever is highest. A supertall podium with tall retail, lobby and transit storeys can put the 4th storey top well above 12 m, so the zone is computed from Layer 0 storey levels; 12 m and 16 m are comparators.
flags.detail: Sources P05-S21, P05-S22. Team illustration: 24 m zone on a 448 m perimeter = 10,752 m2.

flags.claim: Bird-glazing percentages (Toronto 85%, UBC 90%, 85%, 55%) and marker spacings apply to the VTC tower.
flags.correction: Vancouver's guidelines are voluntary for development permits and set no percentage; only the risk-zone rule and marker gaps are Vancouver text. Toronto and UBC numbers were read at source; CSA A460:19 was not opened.
flags.detail: CDDG (effective 27 Oct 2026) and RPSLD A.4.1(e) require a response to the guidelines, not a number. Sources P05-S21, P05-S32, P05-S34, P05-S33, P05-S04.

flags.claim: The consolidated VTC block is R019 Site Type C (single parcel).
flags.correction: R019 defines Type C as a single-parcel large site that occasionally qualifies under the Higher Buildings Policy, usually over an excavated parkade, which supports the choice. Several towers under separate permits with most open space on structure suggest Type B (15-20% canopy, 40% cover).
flags.detail: Editable in P05-M01 and P05-M02. Source P05-S05.

flags.claim: Soil-limited crown credit, size-class soil presets, interior-planting distance d, the 23:00 interior-light hour, migration lights-out dates and the life-safety gate list are team constructs.
flags.correction: Each is editable and labelled TEAM ASSUMPTION; no Vancouver source gives these numbers. The soil preset scales Toronto's 30 m3 by the UFS 50 m2 crown assumption (0.6 m3 per m2).
flags.detail: Affects P05-M02, M03 and M05. Sources P05-S34, P05-S25, P05-S21.

flags.claim: Vancouver uses an urban greening factor, biotope area factor or similar area-weighted index.
flags.correction: None found. No such index appears in the ODP, the draft CDDG, the Green Buildings Policy, the Rezoning Policy for Sustainable Large Developments, R019 or the Building By-law; Vancouver uses canopy % and vegetative-cover % by site type, CSLA soil depths and the rainwater by-law. This is absence of evidence from text searches, so confirm with a City planner.
flags.detail: London UGF (recalled, unverified: 0.4 residential, 0.3 commercial), Berlin BAF, Seattle Green Factor and Singapore Green Plot Ratio pages could not be opened or were not located. Sources P05-S01, P05-S08, P05-S38.

flags.claim: The CDDG text read is final.
flags.correction: The text opened is Appendix A marked DRAFT in the 28 July 2026 Council report; the City says final guidelines will be posted and take effect 27 October 2026 (only the council report was linked on 21 Oct 2026). Re-check clause numbers (S4.5.1, G4.5.x, S1.7.1, S3.9.1, 4.9, 4.10) against the final.
flags.detail: Sources P05-S08, P05-S09.

flags.claim: 'City in Nature' has an official, measurable definition.
flags.correction: The City cites ODP policy L2.3.1 (space for nature; views and connections) in its engagement exhibit, but no numeric measure exists and the clause was not found in the adopted or draft ODP text, so its location is unverified (it may follow Vancouver Plan 2022 numbering). The M01 composite is a team construct and weights are team assumptions.
flags.detail: Sources P05-S41, P05-S01.

flags.claim: Green-roof runoff reductions can be applied to the tower podium and roofs directly.
flags.correction: Roehr and Kong (29% and 58% annual) is modelled for Vancouver at 150 mm medium. The EPA's 60-100% is event-based and US-centric. Do not mix them; use the City figures and state the depth.
flags.detail: Sources P05-S18, P05-S19, P05-S40.

flags.claim: ODP Map 7 ecological corridors create site obligations or can be used as a dataset.
flags.correction: Corridor alignments are conceptual and subject to change; ESA identification adds no new regulation; the map is an image and the open-data catalogue returned no ecological-network layer.
flags.detail: Sources P05-S01, P05-S03, P05-S30.

flags.claim: A flashing-only obstruction-light configuration can be used on the VTC tower to reduce bird collisions.
flags.correction: Standard 621 s.5.4 describes a flashing-only configuration to reduce bird fatalities for towers and similar skeletal structures; whether Transport Canada accepts it for a building is not stated in the text read. Ask Transport Canada.
flags.detail: Standard text read in part (200,000 of 233,211 characters). Source P05-S43.

flags.claim: The Re-Wilding Strategy and the Public Views Guidelines add no further numeric ecology or view requirements for this block.
flags.correction: RPSLD A.4.1(e) asks for a response to the Re-Wilding Strategy (the Rewilding Action Plan 2014 was not located) and CDDG 4.10 sends view-cone sites to the Public Views Guidelines (10 July 2024, not opened). Content unknown.

flags.claim: Thresholds exist for wind and sun hours on terraces, tree anchorage at height, CSLA soil depths, and heat-island performance in Vancouver.
flags.correction: None found in the sources opened; the P05-M03 and P05-M06 values are editable presets or borrowed comparators and are labelled. The life-safety gates need a registered professional.
flags.detail: See unresolved_relationships.

unresolved_relationships: Soil volume per tree versus achievable mature crown area for trees over structure: CSLA depths are paywalled and unopened; the IRMP toolkit gives lawn and rain-garden depths only; RPSLD A.3.8 says staff set a case-by-case performance standard. Size-class presets and the crown-credit factor are team assumptions.

Wind speed at terrace height versus plant survival and tree anchorage loads: the City Green Roof Guide is qualitative and no Canadian standard for tree anchorage at height was found; needs a CLIM wind study plus a wind or structural engineer.
Direct sun hours versus plant class (full sun, part shade): no Vancouver source found; presets would follow horticultural convention and must be flagged team assumption.

Effect of night lighting, obstruction-light type and height on bird collision rate for a 244-305 m tower: the Explanatory Note says collision extent has not been scientifically assessed; Standard 621 gives a flashing-only option for towers, not confirmed for buildings; Machtans gives only national shares.

Quantified effect of podium and tower-top greening on pedestrian-level temperature on this site: InVEST weights are general; no Vancouver coefficient found; would need UMEP/SOLWEIG or ENVI-met style simulation.
Whether non-potable reuse storage can count toward the By-law detention volume: not stated in the by-law text opened; ask rainwater@vancouver.ca.
Minimum albedo, reflectance or SRI for Vancouver roofs and paving: no City requirement found; Toronto values (now voluntary) used as presets.

Stepping-stone distance or patch-size thresholds for a 1.15 ha block to function as ecological connection to Stanley Park: the City defines cores, stepping stones and corridors but gives no numeric criteria.
Species-specific mature crown growth rates and time to maturity in Vancouver conditions (R019 says forecast at maturity without a table).
Reflectance or threat-factor limits for glazing (for example ABC material threat factor, visible-light reflectance): not opened; CSA A460:19 is paywalled.

Location and wording of ODP policy L2.3.1 'City in nature, nature in the city': cited in the HBPR exhibit p.6 but not found in the adopted or draft ODP plain text; check the Vancouver Plan 2022 text or ask a City planner.

How to count trees in view from floors above about 10-15 storeys (team estimate): the 3-30-300 paper gives no viewing distance or upper-floor rule; an angular-size minimum is an alternative to the 30 m buffer.

Whether and how a VTC tower may enter the QE Park view cone or other protected views under the Public Views Guidelines (10 July 2024, not opened) and the Higher Buildings Policy; owned by the SITE packet.
Park dedication area the Park Board would require for a 1.15 ha site (RPSLD A.3.1, 1.1 ha per 1,000 residents metric to be updated): case by case; affects buildable area and canopy base.
Content of the Re-Wilding Strategy / Rewilding Action Plan 2014 that RPSLD A.4.1(e) asks applicants to respond to: not located or opened.
